title: KUBE-MARK-DROP and KUBE-MARK-MASQ ownership changed

detection.reason: host iptables chains are not Kubernetes objects; nothing in the collected inventory, and no read-only kubectl query, shows which components write rules that jump to these chains

quote: The `IPTablesOwnershipCleanup` feature (KEP-3178) is now GA; kubelet no longer creates the `KUBE-MARK-DROP` chain (which has been unused for several releases) or the `KUBE-MARK-MASQ` chain (which is now only created by kube-proxy).
remediation: Only matters if something outside kube-proxy writes iptables rules jumping to `KUBE-MARK-MASQ` or `KUBE-MARK-DROP` — some CNI plugins and node agents do. Those chains now exist only while kube-proxy runs; a rule that jumps to a missing chain is a startup error for whatever installs it.
